quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel results briefing Q&A: 1Q of FY2026 IR Briefing Summary of Q&A (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A, CFO Takahiko Iwai presenting): in the standalone domestic steel business the company projects a profit of JPY 120 billion in 2H FY2026, recovering from zero in 1H, aiming for an annualized rate of JPY 240 billion; achieving it requires continued pass-through of higher external costs via steel price revisions, in particular the JPY 15,000 per-ton price increase in distribution sales. By further implementing that increase toward 2H the company believes it can reach JPY 200 billion or more (the benchmark in the 2030 Mid- to Long-Term Management Plan); JPY 200 billion from the standalone domestic steel business plus JPY 200 billion from steel group companies and JPY 100 billion from non-steel would maintain the domestic business medium-term target of JPY 500 billion or more. Management says the distribution price increase is roughly halfway implemented, will be accelerated into 2H, and that the JPY 100 billion price improvement from 1H to 2H is fully achievable (price revisions to specific customers and distribution sales plus a richer high-value-added mix).
quarterly_data.figure: 2H FY2026 standalone domestic steel profit JPY 120 billion (annualized JPY 240 billion); JPY 15,000 per-ton distribution price increase roughly halfway implemented; domestic target JPY 500 billion or more

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel results briefing Q&A: 1Q of FY2026 IR Briefing Summary of Q&A (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the 1Q average steel sales price declined to JPY 142,000 per ton from JPY 143,000 per ton in 4Q of the previous fiscal year because of a temporary deterioration in product mix (lower shipments of certain high-value-added products due to inventory adjustments) and a timing gap in reflecting raw material and fuel cost increases into prices under differing customer contract structures. On anti-dumping: provisional AD duty is already imposed on stainless steel and galvanized steel sheets (GI); for hot-rolled and cold-rolled sheets, investigated since June 2026, the company has not identified specific changes in customer purchasing behavior and will monitor circumvention imports and front-loaded imports. Domestic strategy: no additional structural reforms in Japan are assumed under the 2030 plan; the next-generation hot-strip mill at Nagoya Works is to lift cost and quality competitiveness for ultra-high-tensile automotive sheet, focused on the Chubu region, aiming to secure JPY 200 billion or more a year from the domestic steel business over the medium term.
quarterly_data.figure: 1Q average sales price JPY 142,000 per ton (4Q JPY 143,000 per ton)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel results briefing Q&A: 1Q of FY2026 IR Briefing Summary of Q&A (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: U.S. Steel (results briefing Q&A): the flat first-half / second-half underlying business profit outlook assumes a certain degree of decline in U.S. steel prices in 2H and includes the seasonal winter downturn in the mining business in 4Q; management says higher-than-assumed HRC prices would be upside and, with stable operations, sees potential for further upside from FY2027. The synergy target for this fiscal year was raised from $200 million to $300 million, reflecting an additional $100 million from shop-floor improvements (blast-furnace stabilisation know-how such as optimised hot-blast temperature, steelmaking yield gains and lower auxiliary-material use, better hot-rolling strip threading). Management says the break-even point has been improving and cannot be estimated from HRC prices alone (mixed products; fixed-price and market-linked contracts), and aims to lower it structurally including through the $2.5 billion capital investment plan; rising fixed costs are in line with the 2030 plan, U.S. Steel is expected to contribute positively to net income this fiscal year, and the next one to two years are a critical period until the capital investments deliver.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. Steel synergy target raised to $300 million (from $200 million); $2.5 billion capital investment plan
